text: As recruits cry aloud when only slightly wounded, and shudder more at the hands of the surgeon than at the sword, while veterans even when transfixed allow their hurts to be dressed without a groan, and as patiently as if they were in some one else's body, so now you ought to offer yourself courageously to be healed.
author: Lucius Annaeus Seneca
locator: Of Consolation, to his Mother Helvia, Chapter 3
